chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: Illinois Jacquet and Calvin Jackson at the Swing Club
summary: Meeting Illinois Jacquet, who tried to recruit him, and pianist Calvin Jackson sitting in.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Going back to the Swing Club on Hollywood Boulevard and Las Palmas for a minute, because I have so many great memories from there. That's where I first met Illinois Jacquet. When I came here with Ernie Fields, he had his group with his brother Russell. They were playing. And he tried to persuade me to join his band. Because we had a lot of fun playing together, I'd go out and sit in with him, you know.

I also heard Calvin Jackson for the first time; he sat in with us at Billy Berg's. You know, Calvin Jackson, the great pianist and conductor. At the time, he was under contract to MGM as a musical director. This was in 1945.

Maybe so, yeah. But I knew he was at the time. And on Charlie Parker's off-night, he came in and sat in with us for the first time since he had been Billy Berg's, you know, there on Longtree and Vine. Those were some of the little treats that were happening during that time, you know.
